pillar_reactions.evidence: Agreed without friction and contributed rather than questioned — when the rep described the daily mobility protocols the prospect supplied the phrase himself, 'motion is lotion', and then volunteered his own parallel practice: 'have you ever heard of rope flow before?... it's very much this practice that is designed for mobility and learning how to just use the body as a unit.' He had already validated the training claim on his own body from the free content: 'I've been really feeling the, like, full-body-working-as-one-unit thing. And it's like, I never felt that in the weight room, ever.' The pillar had almost nothing to prove.

No pushback on the what/when/how-much frame, but two substantive mechanics questions, both of which he raised himself. On alcohol: 'what is his approach to alcohol... what his take is on no alcohol during the six months.' On tour catering: 'usually when I go on the road, that's all I'm eating completely catered food that I don't have control over... from September through December.' The first was answered well, the second only partially, and the prospect flagged it as an unresolved caveat rather than accepting the answer.

By some distance the strongest reaction of the call and the thing that closed it: 'I'm honestly really, like, that excites me big time.' He then tied it directly to his own stated goal and to lived experience of group accountability — 'I don't actually enjoy the pressure of it, but the fruit, the reward of it is worth it to me' — and produced a concrete scene of what he is buying: 'when I just finished half of my day, and I have a break, and I'm tired, and I want to go take a nap, I have 40 minutes to give right now, and I'm going to do it, even if I'm dragging... it's 97 degrees outside and it's hot as, and I'm tired... Like, we're doing this right now.' The rep followed with the what-does-it-feel-like question and got the purchase rationale in one line: 'I like that guy, that guy can stick it through.'

anchors.raw: pretty much every day for, since probably July... have been doing kettlebell stuff, just literally Trevor's workouts. I'll just find them on YouTube. And my sleep has gotten immensely better. Literally within a week and a half.
anchors.note: The most important anchor on this call and it was never addressed. The prospect is already executing the coach's own free programming and getting measurable results — better sleep, faster mornings, whole-body engagement he had never felt in a weight room. That is a live and entirely reasonable argument for not paying $6,000. He talked himself past it on his own ('I can only get so much out of that... I want a coach'), but the rep never engaged with it, and at scale this is the objection the free content manufactures for every inbound lead it produces.

anchors.raw: because I've been taking the summer off, and I haven't had income since May, I feel more drawn to being able to finance it, or draw it out
anchors.note: Three months without income at the point of purchase, with earnings not resuming until September, against a schedule of three $2,000 payments starting immediately. He has a 750 credit score and chose the interest-free option, so this is a cashflow timing issue rather than an affordability one — but two of the three payments land inside the window he had just described as having no income, and nobody checked.

anchors.raw: I also travel. So it's like, you know, I can't necessarily afford multiple gym memberships or to bring a bunch of equipment with me.
anchors.note: Cost sensitivity stated openly about a comparatively trivial expense, at the same moment he was describing why the modality appealed. Recorded because it sits oddly against a $6,000 purchase and marks him as a genuinely price-constrained buyer who bought anyway on the strength of the identity pitch rather than the economics.

anchors.raw: I was also starting to do more research online YouTube and all that found Trevor's work and was like this looks so freaking Fun... I've never like looked at working out as fun.
anchors.note: Fifth prospect in this batch to arrive pre-sold by the content. The specific hook here was novel — the work looked enjoyable rather than effective — which is a different value proposition from the time-efficiency and longevity angles the rep leads with elsewhere and may be worth testing deliberately.

unmet_demand.want: A workable nutrition approach for four or five nights a week of employer-catered tour food he has no control over, from September to December
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep offered guidelines and suggested sourcing his own food nearby, which does not cover the nights when that is impossible and which the prospect had already described as 'a pain in the to do'. Half the six-month term falls inside this constraint. He explicitly parked it rather than accepting the answer — 'just to put that on the table, that is one caveat to the nutrition part of it.'

unmet_demand.want: Confirmation that his existing rope flow practice fits alongside the programme rather than conflicting with it
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep had not heard of it and loosely equated it to Trevor's lymphatic movements and to animal flow without establishing whether they overlap, compete for recovery, or should both be kept. The prospect intends to do it daily regardless — 'I will also be doing that every day' — so an unreconciled second modality is going into the programme unannounced to the coach.

unmet_demand.want: A clear programme position on alcohol for the six months, asked for directly
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no policy, so the rep gave his personal practice instead — ten years without drinking — prefaced with 'he cannot prohibit anything.' Honest and well handled, but it means a client asking what the programme expects of him receives an individual's opinion rather than a standard. Worth defining given it is the second undocumented policy question in this batch.
